code:
(define (make-counter)
  (let ((count 0))           ; the environment the closure captures
    (lambda ()               ; the lambda forms the closure
      (set! count (+ count 1))
      count)))

(define counter1 (make-counter))
(define counter2 (make-counter))

(counter1)                   ; 1
(counter1)                   ; 2
(counter2)                   ; 1
(counter1)                   ; 3
description: You can follow captured state across repeated function calls.

steps.description: make-counter binds count to zero and returns a lambda that can still access it. This returned function and its captured environment form a closure.
You call make-counter twice to create separate counters. Calling counter1 twice updates its count and returns 1, then 2.

steps.answer: It returns 1. Its captured count started at zero and is separate from counter1's count.
steps.question: What does counter2 return on its first call?

steps.description: You see counter2 return 1 and counter1 then return 3. The output 1, 2, 1, 3 shows each closure retaining its own state.

title: Two independent counter closures
